gold_insights.insight: By 2025, ~20% share for NEVs in annual new vehicle sales and average electricity consumption of new passenger BEVs ≤ 12.0 kWh/100 km; by 2035, BEVs become the mainstream of new vehicle sales.

Plan 2021–2035 shifts from direct subsidies for NEVs to taxation exemptions (e.g., no vehicle purchase tax and no vehicle and vessel tax), charging subsidies, and parking incentives, and incentivizes R&D investment from state-owned enterprises.

Plan 2021–2035 tightens the NEV vehicle market entrance requirements and accelerates the elimination of zombie companies that reap subsidies through forged sales documents, and expands the regulatory and technical requirements to include smart driving, shared mobility, and other emerging industries.
Plan 2021–2035 requires establishing the power battery traceability and management platform for NEVs and accelerating legislation on spent power batteries to enhance battery reuse and recycling.

Plan 2021–2035 sets short- and long-term requirements for charging and battery swapping infrastructure, including incorporating deployment into urban and rural planning, grid planning, residential property management, and urban parking management; promoting location-oriented facilities (smart, slow-charging in residential areas supplemented by fast-charging, and fast-charging along highways in urban and rural areas supplemented by slow-charging); and forming compatible charging service platforms with information sharing and a uniform method of payment.

Plan 2021–2035 aims to commercialize FCVs and build the foundation for a hydrogen fuel supply system by 2035; Task 4 encourages deploying hydrogen fuel refill supporting systems based on existing infrastructure used for gasoline, natural gas, or electricity and lowering the cost of hydrogen production, storage, and transport premised on secured safety.
Starting in 2021, ≥ 80% NEVs in new or renewal public fleets in pilot zones and key air pollution regions, and by 2035, 100% electrification of the stock of public fleets.

Plan 2021–2035 encourages increased openness and the deepening of international cooperation, including corporate cooperation with foreign firms, research institutes, and industry associations; strengthening supporting services for international cooperation such as corporate compliance and legal consulting and test and certification services; and proactively participating in making the relevant international rules and standards.
